entries.title: Psalms 61:2
segments:
From the end of the earth; this psalm was probably written when David was an exile from the sanctuary.  Separation from God's presence seemed to him like banishment to the ends of the earth. 
 
God is a sure refuge, in all times of trouble, to those who pray to and put their trust in him.

entries.title: Psalms 61:3
segments: A strong tower; place and means of defence.

entries.title: Psalms 61:4
segments: I will abide in thy tabernacle; or, let me abide in thy tabernacle. to abide in God's tabernacle is to be admitted to commuion with him as a member of his household.  Of this the visible tabernacle service was a sign and a pledge.  See notes to

entries.title: Psalms 61:5
segments:
The heritage of those that fear thy name; the presence and blessing of God. 
 
God witnesses the engagements and hears the supplications of his people, and none truly seek him in vain.

entries.title: Psalms 61:7
segments: He shall abide before God for ever; probably an allusion to the promise made by God to David through Nathan: "Thy house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee."
However great or long continued their trials, the people of God are ripening for heaven and preparing to dwell with him for ever.

entries.title: Psalms 61:8
segments: My vows; his engagements to serve the Lord.
